Status: I reviewed `auth.controller.ts`, `auth.service.ts`, `email.service.ts`, and Supabase setup. The errors you’re seeing come directly from Supabase’s auth rules.

What’s happening
- Login 401 "Email not confirmed": Supabase blocks `signInWithPassword` for unverified users. Our `signIn` simply surfaces Supabase’s error.
- Forgot-password 400 "User not allowed": Supabase won’t issue a recovery link for unverified users. Our `sendPasswordResetEmail` forwards that error.

How to resolve now
- Verify the user’s email first, then both login and forgot-password will work.
  - Click the verification link sent on signup, which redirects to `FRONTEND_URL/verify-email`, then your frontend calls `POST /api/auth/verify-email` with the token.
  - Ensure `FRONTEND_URL` is correct in env (e.g., `https://arzansite.com` or your local URL) so the link works.
  - Confirm SMTP is working (logs from `EmailService` show “SMTP server is ready to send emails” and “Email sent successfully”).

If you need unblocked testing
- Temporary: enable unconfirmed sign-ins in your Supabase project (not recommended for production).
- Or create and confirm a test user via the existing flow.

Optional improvements I can add
- Map Supabase errors to clearer messages:
  - On login, convert “Email not confirmed” → 401 with a friendly message prompting verification.
  - On forgot-password, convert “User not allowed” → 400 “Please verify your email before resetting password.”
- Add an endpoint to resend the verification email for an unconfirmed account.

Say the word if you want me to implement the error mapping and a `resend-verification` endpoint.

- Verified that `POST /api/auth/login` calls `signInWithPassword` and directly returns Supabase’s “Email not confirmed” error.

### Short answer
- It’s a backend configuration issue, not a frontend bug.
- Your backend is calling Supabase Admin endpoints without a valid service_role context, most likely because `SUPABASE_URL` and/or `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` are misconfigured.

### What the logs mean
- “this token needs to have one of the following roles: service_role” on POST `/admin/users` means a request hit Supabase Admin API without a service role token.
- The follow-up “User not allowed” on `POST /api/auth/signup` is your backend surfacing Supabase’s admin/createUser failure.

### Why this is happening
- In `SupabaseService`, we use `createClient(supabaseUrl, serviceRoleKey, ...)` for admin actions.
- If `SUPABASE_URL` is wrong or points to your own API (e.g. `https://api.arzansite.com`), the SDK will send admin calls to the wrong host, and the token will be treated as non-admin.
- If `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is missing/invalid or from a different Supabase project than `SUPABASE_URL`, Supabase will reject admin endpoints.
- If the frontend is accidentally calling Supabase Admin endpoints (never do this from the browser), you will also see this exact error.

### What to fix
- Set the correct Supabase values in your `.env` used by the container:
  - SUPABASE_URL = your Supabase project URL like `https://xxxxxxxxxxxx.supabase.co` (not your API domain)
  - SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY = the Service Role key from Supabase > Project Settings > API
  - SUPABASE_ANON_KEY = the anon public key (frontend only)
  - SUPABASE_JWKS_URL = `https://xxxxxxxxxxxx.supabase.co/auth/v1/keys`

- Ensure the frontend never calls any Supabase Admin endpoints. The frontend should only:
  - Call your backend endpoints (`/api/auth/signup`, `/api/auth/login`, etc.), or
  - Use Supabase client with the anon key for user auth flows that do not require admin privileges.

- Redeploy backend so the container picks up the fixed env:
  - `docker-compose down && docker-compose up --build -d`

- Then:
  - Sign up → user receives email → verify email → login works.
  - Forgot password only works for confirmed emails (Supabase requirement). If unconfirmed, you’ll get the “User not allowed” response.

If you send me your current `.env` (redact secrets except to confirm the host patterns), I’ll validate them. I can also add a “resend verification email” endpoint and friendlier error messages if you’d like.

- Root cause: backend misconfigured `SUPABASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, or frontend calling admin endpoints directly.
- Confirmed in code: `SupabaseService` expects `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`; `AuthService.signUp` uses `auth.admin.createUser`.
- Action: Fix `.env` to real Supabase project URL and service role key; rebuild; ensure frontend does not call admin APIs.

Status: I reviewed your backend’s Supabase integration and the auth flow. The errors are due to how Supabase is being called and envs set when using your self-hosted instance at `api.arzansite.com`.

### What the error means
- The log for `POST /admin/users` with “this token needs to have one of the following roles: service_role” is coming from Supabase. It happens when an Admin endpoint is hit with a non–service_role token (typically anon).
- Your frontend login 401 (“Email not confirmed”) is Supabase’s expected behavior until the user verifies their email.
- The 400 (“User not allowed”) on forgot-password also happens for unverified users.

### Root causes
- Frontend is still calling Supabase Admin (or signup) directly, or
- Backend doesn’t have the correct service role env loaded, so its Admin call is using anon.

### How to wire this architecture
You want: NestJS handles signup and all emails with your templates; Supabase still issues tokens.

Backend (NestJS):
- Use your self-hosted Supabase in env:
  - SUPABASE_URL = `https://api.arzansite.com`
  - SUPABASE_JWKS_URL = `https://api.arzansite.com/auth/v1/keys`
  - SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY = your service role key from the self-hosted project
  - FRONTEND_URL = your frontend origin (e.g., `https://arzansite.com`)
- Make sure the container actually sees these values (compose passes `.env`; rebuild/restart after changes).
- Keep using existing endpoints:
  - `POST /api/auth/signup` → uses `auth.admin.createUser` and sends custom verification email
  - `POST /api/auth/verify-email` → verifies token via Supabase
  - `POST /api/auth/login` → returns Supabase access/refresh tokens
  - `POST /api/auth/forgot-password` → sends recovery link via your email template

Frontend:
- Do NOT call any Supabase Admin endpoints from the browser. Never expose service role key client-side.
- Replace direct Supabase signup with backend calls:
  - Sign up: call `POST /api/auth/signup`

Status: I reviewed all SQL migrations under `src/migrations`, tightened RLS and function security, fixed an incomplete migration, and made bucket creation idempotent. I also added explicit authorization checks to sensitive SECURITY DEFINER functions and ensured their `search_path` is hardened.

What I changed
- Hardened SECURITY DEFINER functions
  - Added `SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''` to all custom functions used by clients: `has_role`, `get_current_user_role`, `is_email_verified`, `is_email_verification_expired`, `log_email_verification`, `mark_email_verification_success`, `mark_email_verification_failed`, `set_email_verification_expiration`, `handle_email_verification`, `save_design_data`, `get_design_data`, `process_wallet_transaction`, `refund_order_to_wallet`.
  - Ensured functions reference fully-qualified `public.*` tables already in the code.

- RLS and grants tightened
  - `wallets` and `transactions`:
    - Removed client ability to update wallets or insert transactions. Use `process_wallet_transaction`/`refund_order_to_wallet` only.
    - Added authorization checks inside functions: permit only service role tokens (`auth.jwt()->>'role'='service_role'`), the owner (`auth.uid()=user_id`), or admins (`public.has_role(auth.uid(),'admin')`).
    - Added REVOKE/GRANT EXECUTE only to `authenticated` and `service_role`.
  - `design_data`:
    - Removed client insert/update policies; now writes must go via `save_design_data` which checks owner/admin/service_role authorization.
  - `payment_transactions`:
    - Removed client insert policy; server handles inserts.
  - `email_logs` and `email_verification_logs`:
    - Restricted inserts to service role via `WITH CHECK ((auth.jwt() ->> 'role') = 'service_role')`.
    - Allowed users to read only their own records; admins can read all (via `user_roles`).
    - Revoked public grants; granted only necessary privileges.
  - `profiles`:
    - Consolidated the “Users can only access verified accounts” policy to use `public.is_email_verified(user_id)` or admin role; dropped duplicates before creating.

- Triggers and idempotency
  - Dropped and recreated triggers where needed to avoid duplicate creation on re-run.
  - Storage buckets creation made idempotent using DO blocks with `unique_violation` handling.
  - Ensured `pgcrypto` extension creation (idempotent) for UUID/generate functions.

- Fixed incomplete migration
  - Replaced the orphaned `REVOKE` in `20250730000000-email-system.sql` with a safe no-op and ensured `pgcrypto` exists.

Why this is safer in production
- Prevents client-side privilege escalation by disallowing direct DML on sensitive tables; enforces server-validated logic.
- SECURITY DEFINER functions cannot be hijacked via `search_path`.
- Only service role or the correct authenticated principal can mutate critical data (wallet balances, payment transactions, design data).
- Email logging endpoints cannot be spammed by clients to forge logs; only service role inserts.

What you should do next
- Apply migrations to your self-hosted Supabase (in order). If you use a runner, point it at `src/migrations/`.
- Ensure your backend uses the service role key when performing server functions (already true via `SupabaseService`).
- Frontend should avoid direct writes to `wallets`, `transactions`, `design_data`, `email_logs` — call backend endpoints which invoke the server functions.
- Verify:
  - New signup → verification email → `verify-email` route → login succeeds.
  - Attempt client-side inserts/updates on protected tables fail with RLS errors.
  - `save_design_data`, wallet deposit/payment/refund via server paths succeed.
